summary: The purpose of virtual, augmented and mixed reality, the hardware they need, and how they are used in education, medicine, industry and entertainment.

items.title: Virtual reality (VR)
items.content: A fully **computer-generated 3D world** that replaces what the user sees and hears. The user is **immersed** and can look around and interact.

items.title: Augmented reality (AR)
items.content: **Computer-generated images, text or sounds are added on top of the real world**, seen through a phone, tablet or smart glasses.

items.title: Mixed reality (MR)
items.content: Virtual objects are **anchored in the real world** and the user can interact with them as if they were real (e.g. Microsoft HoloLens, Apple Vision Pro).

blocks.title: Hardware
rows: Head-mounted display (headset) with a screen for each eye
Smartphone/tablet camera and screen
Motion sensors: gyroscope, accelerometer, head and hand tracking
Camera + GPS + compass + accelerometer to know position and direction
Hand controllers, data gloves, haptic (vibration) feedback
Smart glasses (head-up display)
Powerful computer / GPU to render the scene
Software that recognises surfaces and markers
Education
Virtual field trips (space, history, inside the human body); virtual laboratories with dangerous experiments
3D models appear over the textbook; labels on real objects
Training
Flight and driving simulators; surgery practice; firefighter and military training — safe, repeatable, cheap per session
Step-by-step repair instructions over a real engine
Medicine
Treating phobias and PTSD; pain distraction; rehabilitation games
Showing veins or organs over the patient during surgery
Architecture and design
Walking through a building before it is built
Seeing new furniture in your own room (IKEA Place)
Retail and tourism
Virtual stores and museums
Virtual try-on of glasses/clothes; information about sights through the camera
Entertainment
Immersive games, virtual concerts
Pokémon GO, Snapchat filters
Navigation
Arrows drawn over the street view; head-up displays in cars

blocks.title: Advantages and disadvantages
rows: Safe practice of dangerous or expensive tasks
VR headsets are expensive and need powerful hardware
Makes abstract ideas visible and memorable
Motion sickness, eye strain, headaches
Remote collaboration and visits without travel
Isolation from real people (VR); distraction and accidents (AR)
Engaging and motivating for learners
Content is expensive to create; privacy of camera data

blocks.content: "Explain the purpose" — say **what problem it solves**: "VR lets trainee pilots **practise emergency situations safely** without risking an aircraft or lives."
